pr.title: Item categories and a category filter on the list

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0003_item_categories.sql implements it; test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks rows, UNIQUE and CHECK failures, nullable column, index and tagged items.
test 'AC-2' inserts title-only (null category_id) and asserts an unknown category_id throws FOREIGN KEY.

test 'AC-3' asserts id order, categorised markup and '
  • No category
    • '; src/index.js `item`.
test 'AC-4' asserts the exact link list/hrefs in NOCASE order including an empty category, and only All current.
tests 'AC-5' check Work-only items in id order, Work current, and that &x=1 / ?x=1 pages are identical to the base pages.
test 'AC-6' asserts 200, 'No items in this category.', no <li>, and the current link.
test 'AC-7' asserts the escaped label, the encoded href, and that following the link lists the item.
it.each 'AC-8' covers all five bad URLs: 404, message, Go back href '/', referrer script, no <li>, no <nav>.

Verified by review as the spec allows. The review step is concrete. The script in brokenLinkPage calls history.back() for a same-origin referrer and otherwise leaves the href '/', so an empty referrer throws in `new URL` and falls through. Matches the spec flow. The extra `history.length > 1` guard is harmless.

routes.json lists /?category=Work. tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers accepting a query and rejecting whitespace, # and a missing slash. test/traffic.test.js asserts ROUTES contains it and the fake app sees path+query. The index test 'AC-11' asserts every route answers ok.
The existing healthz, 404, 405, escaping and empty-table tests are unchanged except the First item assertion, which now uses the AC-3 markup. The tests could not be run here: vitest is not installed.
test/apply-migrations.js drops in one batch with defer_foreign_keys. Test 'AC-13' asserts the count is 4 after the earlier tests leave categorised rows. It is weak but would fail if the reset broke.

findings.what: The States table is only partly tested. No test asserts 'Go back' is hidden on any 200 state (rows 1-4). The 'No items yet.' test (`/`, no items) does not check that the filter links show with All current. The unfiltered list and known-category pages are never checked for the absence of the broken-link message.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, assert the nav links and All current, and that 'Go back' and 'corrupted' are absent. In the AC-3, AC-5 and AC-6 tests, assert 'Go back' is absent.

findings.what: The diff includes a new no-op migration, 0002_reset_to_baseline-3.sql (`SELECT 1`), from the baseline reset commit. The PR body does not mention it.
findings.fix: Mention it in the PR body, or confirm it belongs to the base.

findings.what: The Go-back script adds a `history.length > 1` condition that the spec does not list. The spec only rejected using it as the sole test, so this is harmless but unspecified.
findings.fix: Drop the extra guard or record it in the spec.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent: item categories plus a list filter. Nothing was added beyond the spec, apart from the extra history.length guard.
All 13 items are met. The spec go commit comes before the implementation commits and only recorded the owner's acceptance. No acceptance item was edited after the go.

vitest is not installed here, so npm test could not run. That goes in this note, not as a finding. Tests name their ACs and would fail if the code were wrong. The State-table gaps are in the findings.
README now describes the filter and the 404. CLAUDE.md and the README already say new features add routes to routes.json. Nothing found stale.
Matching, encoding and escaping are correct. The traffic Worker passes the query through. The only finding is the unspecified history.length guard.
Names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded. Queries are parameterised. The inline script uses no user input. No planted instructions found.
The diff changes the HTML in src/index.js (nav, list and 404 page). The structure is plain and spec-conformant.
The UI flows are covered by the tests above. The Go-back behaviour (AC-10) was verified by reading the script, not in a browser.
The claims are true of the diff. The traffic regex change is disclosed. The only gap is that the 0002 reset migration is not mentioned.
